description:
List every account on the workspace with its stored balance. Rows only — this tool holds no definition of cash, and returns no figure the app renders.

Use it when you are computing a cash figure whose RULES you are stating yourself: which accounts belong to the business, which account types count as cash, which stored field is "the balance", what each currency converts at. The server derives no cash position of its own from this call, so a cash figure starts here: state the rules, keep exactly the rows they admit, then put the result on a card with `well_render_cash_position` — or, when the answer is cash month by month rather than one total, with `well_render_cash_forecast`.

**It applies no scope.** Every active account comes back, including ones you will almost certainly exclude. `ownership` is `workspace`, `counterparty` or `unknown`, and it decides membership together with `company_id`:

  - `workspace` — the business's own, EXCEPT when `own_company_id` is set AND the row names a company that is neither that anchor nor one of the business's own entities (a company that holds one of its connections is the business itself). A row with no `company_id` is trusted, because a connector tags a row before any holder is known; so is a row naming a company while `own_company_id` is still `null`, because nothing has disproved the pairing yet. Only a tag contradicting a resolved anchor and the own entities is stale, and counting that one widens the owned scope and overstates the figure.
  - `counterparty` — not the business's, unconditionally. A counterparty row's balance, or its absence, is never reported: a `null` there is expected, not a missing reading, and its `cash_exclusion_reason` says nothing to report. Never report its balance gap or its state: do not call it missing, waiting, unclassified or syncing. At most count it.
  - `unknown` — unsettled, and settled ONLY by the anchor: own when `company_id` equals `own_company_id`, a counterparty's when it names a different one.

`own_company_id` is `null` when the workspace has not set one. Nothing is settled against it then — no `unknown` row, and no `workspace` row's company pairing either — so say so rather than counting or dropping on a guess. This is the same three-way rule the app's own canvas account scope applies, and a figure that departs from it disagrees with the number the product shows.

`owned_by_workspace` is that rule already applied by the server, on the anchor and on the business's own entities: `true` is a row the app's own scope counts as the business's. Keep exactly the `true` rows as the business's own accounts and do not re-derive the answer from `ownership` and `company_id`; a `false` row is a counterparty's, an `unknown` row nothing settles, or a stale `workspace` tag.

**It applies no type filter.** `account_type` is one of deposit, credit, loan, investment, payroll, other. A credit or loan account is a liability, so its balance normally nets out of cash rather than adding to it — but that is your decision to state, not a fact about the row, and the sign stored is the sign the provider sent.

**It returns both amounts.** `closing_booked` is SETTLED cash; `closing_value` includes pending and uncleared movements. The two differ by every initiated-but-unsettled payment, so which one you total is the single most consequential choice a cash figure makes: state it. `opening_booked` is the fallback for a freshly-opened balance with no settled activity yet. Any of them is `null` when the stored value was absent or not a finite number, which is not a zero balance.

**One field for every account.** A balance per account is `closing_booked`, or `opening_booked` when `closing_booked` is `null`. Read that same field on every row, deposit, credit and loan alike. Never quote `closing_value` as one account's balance: on a credit or loan account it can hold the provider's available figure (the unused credit line), which is not a balance. Quote `closing_value` only when the person asks for available funds, and then for every account.

**It converts nothing.** Each reading carries its own `currency`, which can differ from the account's own `account_currency`. Convert per row at the stored rate for that currency as of the reading, read from `exchange_rates` and never estimated, then total — a sum across currencies is denominated in nothing and no field here would say it happened.

**It lists each copy of an account.** One physical account can arrive once per connector that syncs it. `duplicate_of_account_id` names the account a row is a second copy of, and is `null` on every other row. Leave a marked row out of every total and every count: the balance that counts is the named account's, which is the one the app's own figure reads, and the transactions of both copies are counted once. Total both copies and the figure holds that money twice. When the named account has no readable balance, report it as having none rather than taking the copy's reading in its place, or the figure departs from the app's. Marking follows the ownership rule above: only the business's own accounts are marked, and an `unknown` row only once `own_company_id` settles it.

`institution_name` is the bank that holds the account: the bank company Well identified, else the bank an accounting tool names for an account it syncs, else the connector that syncs the account. When the person names a bank ("how much at Chase"), keep the rows whose `institution_name` is that bank; `account_name` is the label the provider sends and often does not name the bank.

`source_workspace_connector_id` is the `workspace_connector_id` of the connection that syncs the row, or `null` when no connection does. A live read on that same connection (`well_invoke_connector_tool`, `well_get_investment_holdings`) reads the same money as the row: never add both.

`synced_at` is the source connection's last successful sync time, or `null` when the row has no live synced source. `fresh_enough` is true only when that sync was within the last 24 hours. When a row has a source connection and `fresh_enough` is false, do not present its balance as current: say it may be old or lack a successful sync, name `synced_at` when available, and offer a fresh sync when one is available. When `source_workspace_connector_id` and `synced_at` are both `null`, say that sync age cannot be assessed rather than calling the manual balance stale.

`unlinked_accounts: true` marks a row that carries ZERO weight in cash, and `cash_exclusion_reason` says why. It is present only on such a row, and its value is one of three:

  - `unbound_mirror` — a legacy state: a row the old name rule zeroed before any account evidence. Its weight returns when the one-time re-judge decides it; say it is waiting, not a duplicate.
  - `bound` — an alias of another account in the list; that account, the keeper, carries the weight.
  - `pending` — a row a bank account at the same institution could mirror, not yet decided by the pair judge. It counts for nothing until that is settled, so keep it out and, for a row the ownership rule admits, say it is waiting rather than calling it a duplicate. A counterparty row in this state is not waiting for anything: say nothing about it.

A row with no `cash_exclusion_reason` is counted. Like a `duplicate_of_account_id` row, an excluded row is listed and flagged, never dropped: keep it out of every total and every count, and when you tell the reader what was left out, give its reason in plain words. Its balance still reads as stored.

`balance` is `null` when no row was selected for that account. Two different situations produce it and they must not be reported the same way: `verification_rejected: true` means the newest balance failed verification and the bounded walk back found no verified one, so the data is repudiated; `false` means the account simply has no history yet. This applies to the business's own accounts only: a `counterparty` row's `null` balance is expected, never a reading to report.

`months_back` adds `month_ends` to every row: one reading per complete month end, oldest first, keyed `YYYY-MM`, ending on the last COMPLETE month. This series is where a cash forecast starts — "what will our cash look like", "project our cash forward", "when do we hit zero" — and it is the settled half of `well_render_cash_forecast`; the projected half is that series' last settled month minus the burn you measure with `well_sum_transactions`. A `null` reading is a month no stored row covered — not a zero balance, so never plot it as one and never interpolate between two real points. Omit `months_back` for the current reading alone; the series is a second query and is not free.

`partial: true` means the read was cut short BEFORE RETURNING ANYTHING, so it always arrives with an empty `rows` — stop and offer to try again. `own_set_truncated: true` is different: rows did return, but the workspace's own-company set reached its row cap, so a company missing from that set may still be ours. Continue with the ownership verdicts the server gave, and mark any cash total partial: it is a floor over the known owned accounts. Pass `own_set_truncated` to `well_render_cash_position`; its returned `partial` must be stated. `unreadable_rows` is another separate case that continues: those rows have no usable balance and make any total a floor, by up to their count.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

months_back.description: How many complete month ends to carry per account, oldest first. Omit for the current reading alone.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_list_account_balances

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

fresh_enough.description: Whether the source synced within the last 24 hours.

owned_by_workspace.description: The ownership rule applied by the server: true when the app's own account scope counts the row as the business's.

synced_at.description: The source connection's last successful sync time, or null when no live source sync is recorded.

title: List account balances
